answer: An agent economy curbs Sybil attacks by anchoring identities to estuarine bathymetry. Nodes measure acoustic echo delays off sable benthic silt to track depth shifts driven by the ocean tide. Forging identities requires deploying dedicated sonar hardware across dispersed maritime coordinates, imposing unavoidable equipment and mooring costs. However, severe storm surges disrupt local water levels, causing occasional false rejections of honest nodes.
